I will still do what I mostly did before, because changing too much is risky. On my land, wheat and maize are the steady money, so I will keep most of the ground in that wheat-maize cycle, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton. I watch what the farmers around me do, and if a man cuts fertilizer too hard, the crop shows it fast, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. I have well water, so I will use that when the crop is really asking for it, not just wait for the sky. For wheat, I will put enough base fertilizer in the ground before sowing, then topdress once at jointing, and I will water about three times if the year is normal. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed like most people do now, plant fast after wheat harvest, put the nitrogen a bit heavier because maize eats hard, and water twice if rain is short. Cotton is slower and needs more watching, so I will only keep a smaller patch of it, use improved seed, feed it steady, spray a few more times than grain crops, and not let weeds and insects get ahead of me. That is how I will balance yield, cost, and the labor my family can actually manage.
